annotations.title: Sunset and sunrise: where to stand, and what time to be there

description: Verified East End sunrise and sunset viewpoints, 31 in all: public overlooks, beaches, vineyard lawns, hotel terraces and bars, each with the time. `time` is computed from that spot's own latitude and longitude for the date, on the East End's clock (America/New_York); sunset here swings over three hours across the year, and Orient and Montauk Point differ by about two minutes. Each row also carries `goldenHour` (the hour into sunset, or out of sunrise), `blueHour`, `arriveBy` (30 minutes earlier, when the lot fills), `parking` and `walkDistance`. `startsIn` counts down when it has not happened yet today; `alreadyPassedToday` is set when it has. `when: 'sunrise'` gives the morning side; the default is sunset. `date` (YYYY-MM-DD) computes for another day, and `inBestMonth` says whether that date falls in the months the record names. `wrongWayRound` lists verified spots in the same towns that face the other way (Ditch Plains is east-facing). The data holds no weather. Returns up to 8. `townScope` reports how the place argument was read; `townScope.recognized: false` means the name matched no East End place, the rows array is empty, and `didYouMean` lists near matches where any exist.

date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to compute for. Omit for today, East End local.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. 'dinner', 'drinks', 'no walk', 'wheelchair', 'dog', 'kids', 'vineyard', or a spot's name.

town.description: A hamlet ('Montauk', 'Sag Harbor') or a region ('the Hamptons', 'North Fork'), in the asker's own words.
